items.title: 67425_Tiny Grimes oral history interview
items.q: Maxine Sullivan's been up there, and Bucky Pizzarelli -- guest star, you know.

ctx.x: Car, yeah. But it didn't develop until way late. I was like you make a bruise on your bone, but it don't happen -- after a while it just started developin' -- that's what happened -- on my hip. It really carried me through a thing for a long time with this hip. I couldn't get pain pills at that time, nothin' but aspirin and Empirins. Boy, it was a mess. And I was workin' -- the last place was a place called The Purple Manor, owned by Leon Aikens, he was a good friend of mine. In fact I'm goin' to play the prison…

the sign up there-- and carry a nice review up there every summer. Been goin' up there for quite a while. Maxine Sullivan's been up there, and Bucky Pizzarelli -- guest star, you know. So I'm gonna take a thing up to Lake Placid, or either Raybrook which is near Lake Placid, for the inmates, 'cause I got a call from there and they voted for me to come up. So I'm tryin' to take Ruth Brown and Big Nick Nicholas and my little trio, and probably a shake dancer. I'm gonna do that. It's already in the making. They'll…
Did you ever play a prison before?

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Tiny Grimes, the famous Tiny Grimes with the four string guitar who played with Art Tatum.

ctx.x: Yeah, he was on the bill. Tiny Grimes, the famous Tiny Grimes with the four string guitar who played with Art Tatum. Joe Beck, Chuck Wayne. All the same place. But we knew what we were doing. They were — you know who else was there? Benson. And they were all rehearsing in a corner with Major Holley and a drummer, you know, I want to do this, I want to do that, and I’m saying boy, it’s too late for that. Well that’s the way the business is you know, but we had set groups and we went out there and we played — when…
I’m curious, when you’re working with two guitars like that, and you are going to be doing some substitution chords or something like that, how do you communicate that with your partner?
